skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray with bilateral basal opacities and an implanted cardiac device to determine the primary cause of respiratory symptoms.
steps: Inspect the costophrenic angles and lung bases for blunting or meniscus signs indicative of pleural effusion, and assess for adjacent linear or wedge-shaped opacities suggesting compressive atelectasis.

Differentiate these findings from perihilar alveolar consolidations (which typically present as fluffy, central opacities radiating from the hila) and verify that any visible prosthetic valves appear structurally intact without gross displacement.
